Hi. I'm on holiday, I will review it week after.

The Windows build is failing with

```
FAIL: test_wireshark_capture_from_stdin (suite_capture.case_wireshark_capture)
Capture from stdin using Wireshark
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\builds\wireshark\wireshark\test\fixtures.py", line 54, in wrapped
    test_fn(self, *fixtures)
  File "C:\builds\wireshark\wireshark\test\suite_capture.py", line 496, in test_wireshark_capture_from_stdin
    check_capture_stdin(self, cmd=wireshark_k)
  File "C:\builds\wireshark\wireshark\test\suite_capture.py", line 172, in check_capture_stdin_real
    pipe_proc = self.assertRun(slow_dhcp_cmd + ' | ' + capture_cmd, shell=True)
  File "C:\builds\wireshark\wireshark\test\subprocesstest.py", line 304, in assertRun
    self.assertEqual(process.returncode, expected_return)
AssertionError: 3221225781 != 0
----------------------------------------------------------------------
```
That's the Windows return code for failing to load a DLL.

Current version fails too, but it looks than failure is not related to the code. It says it is not able to load npcap or winpcap DLL:

"dumpcap -D" exited with 2. stderr:
dumpcap: Unable to load Npcap or WinPcap (wpcap.dll); you will not be able to capture packets.

It looks that windows build environment do not match test suite...

> It looks that windows build environment do not match test suite...

The puzzling thing is that the build environment does match the test suite. The other "Windows Build" MR jobs are passing just fine, and have been for a very long time:

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/2698206351
I see, strange. I think my change do not touch dumpcap, but I will double check it...

I created my Windows build environment with Qt6 and even I found other errors, tests passes fine. So I have no idea why does it failing.

Any idea how to proceed?

The Windows MR builds use a container built with this Dockerfile: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/-/blob/master/dev/windows/Dockerfile

I'm busy with SharkFest but will try to do a build in that environment in the next couple of days.

Hi, I successfully build it on Linux (FC35). It looks working, but:
- I see (hear) delay between player cursor and produced sound
- list of audio cards is limited to default one

I will check whether it is caused by Qt features or code.

@geraldcombs: I reviewed patch, I made small changes and now I don't know how to commit my changes back to be part of this MR. Can you advice me?

I made local branch based on your one and then I locally committed to it. But when I would like to:

git push geraldcombs geraldcombs/qt6-multimedia

git says:
To gitlab.com:geraldcombs/wireshark.git
 ! [remote rejected]       geraldcombs/qt6-multimedia -> geraldcombs/qt6-multimedia (deny updating a hidden ref)
error: failed to push some refs to 'gitlab.com:geraldcombs/wireshark.git'

Can you try the following?

- Rename the branch from "geraldcombs/qt6-multimedia" to "qt6-multimedia"
- `git push geraldcombs qt6-multimedia`

Failing that, go ahead and open a new MR and I'll close this one.

git push geraldcombs HEAD:qt6-multimedia

was the right one. Thank you.

I built this MR in a `wireshark-windows-dev:latest` Docker instance and was able to replicate the issue. [Dependencies](https://github.com/lucasg/Dependencies) says:

```
PS C:\wireshark\build> .\deps\Dependencies.exe -chain .\run\RelWithDebInfo\Wireshark.exe -depth 2
├ Wireshark.exe (ROOT) : .\run\RelWithDebInfo\Wireshark.exe
|  ├ libwireshark.dll (ApplicationDirectory) : .\run\RelWithDebInfo\libwireshark.dll
|  |  ├ libwiretap.dll (ApplicationDirectory) : .\run\RelWithDebInfo\libwiretap.dll
|  |  |  ├ libwsutil.dll (ApplicationDirectory) : .\run\RelWithDebInfo\libwsutil.dll
|  |  |  |  ├ glib-2.0-0.dll (ApplicationDirectory) : .\run\RelWithDebInfo\glib-2.0-0.dll

[ ... ]

|  ├ Qt6Multimedia.dll (ApplicationDirectory) : .\run\RelWithDebInfo\Qt6Multimedia.dll
|  |  ├ d3d9.dll (WindowsFolder) : C:\Windows\system32\d3d9.dll
|  |  ├ dxva2.dll (NOT_FOUND) :
|  |  ├ EVR.dll (NOT_FOUND) :
|  |  ├ MF.dll (NOT_FOUND) :
|  |  ├ MFPlat.DLL (NOT_FOUND) :
|  |  ├ MFReadWrite.dll (NOT_FOUND) :
|  |  ├ ole32.dll (WellKnownDlls) : C:\Windows\system32\ole32.dll
|  |  ├ PROPSYS.dll (WindowsFolder) : C:\Windows\system32\PROPSYS.dll
```

It looks like we (specifically I) need to install DirectX in our Windows Docker image. I'll take a look at that in the morning.
As it turns out, installing DirectX in a Server Core container is _exceedingly_ difficult, at least in our case.
I removed Qt6Multimedia from the MR builder and updated `CMakeLists.txt` to make Qt6Multimedia optional.

@@ -1210,12 +1210,13 @@ if(BUILD_wireshark OR BUILD_logray)
 		Qt${qtver}Core
 		Qt${qtver}Gui
 		Qt${qtver}LinguistTools
-		# Our code currently does not compile with Qt6Multimedia
-		# Qt${qtver}Multimedia
 		Qt${qtver}PrintSupport
 		Qt${qtver}Widgets
 		Qt${qtver}Concurrent
 	)
+	set(QT_OPTIONAL_PACKAGELIST
+		Qt${qtver}Multimedia
+	)
 	if(USE_qt6)
 		set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
 		# Setting CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD is not sufficient with MSVC, see
@@ -1226,7 +1227,6 @@ if(BUILD_wireshark OR BUILD_logray)
 		endif()
 		list(APPEND QT_PACKAGELIST Qt6Core5Compat)
 	else()
-		list(APPEND QT_PACKAGELIST Qt5Multimedia)
 		if(WIN32)
 			list(APPEND QT_PACKAGELIST Qt5WinExtras)
 		endif()
@@ -1237,6 +1237,12 @@ if(BUILD_wireshark OR BUILD_logray)
 		list(APPEND QT_INCLUDE_DIRS ${${_qt_package}_INCLUDE_DIRS})
 		list(APPEND QT_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS ${${_qt_package}_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS})
 	endforeach()
+	foreach(_qt_package IN LISTS QT_OPTIONAL_PACKAGELIST)
+		find_package(${_qt_package} ${QT_FIND_PACKAGE_OPTIONS})
+		list(APPEND QT_LIBRARIES ${${_qt_package}_LIBRARIES})
+		list(APPEND QT_INCLUDE_DIRS ${${_qt_package}_INCLUDE_DIRS})
+		list(APPEND QT_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS ${${_qt_package}_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS})
+	endforeach()
 	if(APPLE AND "/usr/local/opt/qt5/lib/QtCore.framework" IN_LIST Qt5Core_INCLUDE_DIRS)
 		# When qt@6 and qt@5 are both installed via Homebrew,
 		# /usr/local/include/QtCore/qvariant.h points to Qt 6 headers.
